title: Security & identity
oneLiner: Default is deny; something must allow and nothing may deny. Audit rules out SSE-S3. Custom rotation or cross-account needs a customer managed key. Same key in two regions means a new multi-region key.

notes.text: How AWS decides: policies and evaluation

notes.html: Default is deny. Something must allow, nothing may explicitly deny, and guardrails (SCPs, boundaries) must not cap it.

notes.html: KMS keys are regional. A multi-region key is a set of related keys in several regions with the same key ID and key material, so data encrypted in one region can be decrypted in another without re-encrypting through KMS.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: No. Create a new multi-region key and its replicas
No new bucket needed: change default encryption to the new key, then re-encrypt existing objects (copy in place or Batch Operations)
S3 replication with SSE-KMS, DynamoDB global tables, cross-region DR, client-side encryption
Each replica has its own key policy and is managed per region

items: Not possible: create a new MRK

questions.q: A company must encrypt S3 objects, have every use of the key logged in CloudTrail, and keep operations to a minimum. Rotation can be AWS's default. What should they use?

options.t: SSE-KMS with the AWS managed key (aws/s3)
options.why: Right. Audited, rotated yearly, nothing to manage.

options.t: SSE-KMS with a customer managed key
options.why: Also works, but more to manage than needed.
You manage keys and send them on every request.

questions.q: Auditors require that the S3 encryption key be rotated every 6 months and that the key can be disabled on demand. What should be used?

options.why: Rotation isn't configurable and you can't disable the key.

options.t: SSE-KMS with the AWS managed key
options.why: Yearly rotation, can't change, can't disable.

options.t: SSE-KMS with a customer managed key
options.why: Right. You set the rotation period (90-2,560 days) and control the key.

options.t: Client-side encryption with the AWS Encryption SDK

questions.q: A bucket in Account A uses SSE-KMS. Users in Account B must read the objects. Which key setup makes this possible?

options.t: The AWS managed key aws/s3, shared with Account B
options.why: You can't change an AWS managed key's policy to share it.

options.t: A customer managed key whose key policy allows Account B, plus IAM permissions in Account B

options.why: Then KMS isn't involved, but the question requires SSE-KMS.

options.t: A new key in Account B
options.why: Account A's objects are encrypted with A's key.

questions.q: A high-traffic bucket using SSE-KMS hits KMS request throttling and high KMS costs. What fixes this with the least change?

options.why: Right. Cuts KMS calls by up to 99%.

questions.q: A company replicates an SSE-KMS bucket to another region and wants the same key ID usable in both. They currently use a single-region customer managed key. What must they do?

options.t: Convert the existing key to multi-region
Create a new multi-region key and a replica in the destination region, then use it for the buckets
Share the key with the other region

questions.q: After creating a new multi-region key, the team wants the existing bucket's objects encrypted with it. What is the least disruptive way?

options.t: Create a new bucket with the key and migrate the app
Set the bucket's default encryption to the new key and re-encrypt existing objects with a copy-in-place (e.g., S3 Batch Operations)

options.why: Rotation keeps the same key; it doesn't switch to the MRK.
Existing objects keep their old key until re-encrypted.

questions.q: Which statement about KMS multi-region keys is true?

options.t: They share the same key ID and material across regions
They're one key object that lives in all regions with one key policy
options.why: Each replica is a separate resource with its own key policy.

options.t: Any existing key can be made multi-region
They are required for all cross-region replication
options.why: Only when you need the same key in both regions; any destination key works for replication.

questions.q: A DR plan needs the application's database credentials available in a second region and kept in sync with rotation. What is the least effort?

options.t: A Lambda that copies the secret every hour

options.why: Right. Native, rotation stays in sync.

options.t: Store the password in Parameter Store in both regions
Put the password in the AMI

questions.q: Security wants to find roles and users with permissions they haven't used in 90 days, across the organization, as findings. What should they use?

options.t: IAM Access Analyzer unused access findings
options.why: Right. It now reports unused roles, keys and permissions.

questions.q: A regulator requires a single-tenant HSM where only the customer has access to the keys, FIPS 140 Level 3. What should be used?

options.t: AWS KMS with customer managed keys
options.why: KMS HSMs are Level 3 validated now, but they're multi-tenant and AWS-operated.
Right. Single-tenant, you control the keys.

questions.q: A company needs HTTPS for an app on EC2 instances behind a load balancer, using a free certificate that renews automatically. What is the recommended design?

options.t: Install an ACM certificate directly on each EC2 instance
options.why: The exam answer: ACM certs aren't used on EC2 (exportable public certs exist since 2025, but they cost money and you renew the install).

options.t: Put the ACM certificate on an ALB and terminate TLS there

questions.q: An app on EC2 must read from DynamoDB. What is the most secure way to give it credentials?

options.t: Store an access key in environment variables
Attach an IAM role through an instance profile

questions.q: The company must stop every member account from launching resources outside eu-west-1 and eu-central-1, including actions by account admins. What should be used?

options.t: An SCP with a Deny when aws:RequestedRegion is not one of the allowed regions
options.why: Right. Applies to everyone in member accounts, including root.

options.t: A permission boundary on every user
options.why: Must be on every identity and admins could remove it.

questions.q: Developers must be able to create IAM roles for their Lambda functions, but those roles must never have more permissions than a defined set. What should be used?

options.why: Caps whole accounts, not developer-created roles specifically.

options.t: A permission boundary that developers must attach to roles they create

questions.q: A mobile app lets users sign in with Google and then upload photos directly to S3. What is the right combination?

options.t: Cognito user pool for sign-in, identity pool to get temporary AWS credentials
An API key in the app

questions.q: A company wants to require login before users reach a web app behind an ALB, using its corporate OIDC identity provider, without changing app code. What should they use?

options.t: ALB listener rule with OIDC authentication

options.why: Needs custom logic to issue them.

questions.q: Which service finds personal data such as credit card numbers in S3 buckets?
The security team needs to scan EC2 instances and container images in ECR for known software vulnerabilities continuously. What should they use?
A team wants to know which S3 buckets, KMS keys and IAM roles are shared with principals outside the organization. What should they use?

options.why: Shows last-accessed times, not external sharing.

options.t: IAM Access Analyzer with the organization as the zone of trust

questions.q: An organization with 80 accounts wants employees to sign in once with their corporate identity provider and get role-based access to the accounts they need. What should be used?

options.t: IAM Identity Center connected to the identity provider, with permission sets

questions.q: Under the shared responsibility model, which task belongs to the customer?

options.t: Patching the guest operating system on EC2
options.why: The OS on EC2 is yours.
AWS applies engine patches in your maintenance window.
